logp.method_description: The n-octanol saturated by water was used as organic phase, and water saturated by n-octanol was used as aqueous phase. Test chemical were weighted accurately to 0.0001 g and added into 25 mL volumetric flask. Then 15.0 mL of organic phase was added, and the flask was shaken to make chemicals dissolved sufficiently. Then we brought to volume by organic phase (the concentration of chemical was controlled as 0.008 mol/L). 10.0 mL of organic solution was brought in a 250 mL ground glass conical flask in which there is 40.0 mL aqueous phase, and then the stopper was plugged. The system was put into an oven controlled crystal oscillator and shaken at 25 °C. Octanol solutions of each compound at a different concentration (0.0008 mol/L) and three flasks for each concentration were prepared to validate the accuracy of the experiment. We tested the concentrations in aqueous phase after 24 h when the equilibrium was achieved. Blanks were prepared in an identical manner, with the exception that no compounds were added. The mixed solution was centrifuged, and the concentration of compounds in aqueous phase and organic phase were determined, respectively, using HPLC(Agilent 1620, USA). Measurements were made at 25 °C, on an Agilent Rx-C18 column (5 μm, 250 × 4.6 mm inner diameter), and analyses were detected with an Agilent1620 Series diode array detector. The mobile phases were mixtures of methanol and 0.5% of tetrafluorine acetic acid with volume ratio 75:25. A flow rate of 1.0 mL/min was adopted and the injection volume was 40 μL. The log P values were calculated as follows: log P = Cn-octanol/Cwater, where, Cn-octanol is the concentration of the test compound in n-octanol phase, Cwater is the concentration of the test compound in water phase.
